name: Har Ki Dun Valley Trek
bestSeason: March to June & Oct to Nov
shortOverview: A cradle of a valley below Swargarohini, reached along river trails, wooden bridges and waterfalls.
fullOverview: Har Ki Dun is a valley trek rather than a summit push, and its appeal is the approach: 35 kilometres of river trails, wooden bridges, dense forest and waterfalls leading into one of Garhwal's most storied valleys. The drive from Dehradun follows the Tons and Yamuna rivers through Purola and Mori to the base at Sankri. From there the route runs to Seema via Gangad on forest trails and riverside paths, then climbs beside the Har Ki Dun River to the Waterfall Camp at around 3,050 m. The finest day walks through alpine meadows and glacial streams into Har Ki Dun Valley at 3,566 m, with Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch, Black Peak and the Jaundar Glacier in view, and an optional hike to Maninda Tal for those with the weather and the legs for it. A buffer day is held in reserve against bad weather, which may take in Osla village and the Someshwar Mahadev Temple.

backpackOffloading: Offload your backpack to a mule or porter to lighten your load during the trek.
Offloading charges range from ₹400 to ₹500 per day per bag.
Ensure your backpack weighs up to 11 kg and is equipped with a waterproof cover.
Suitcases, trolleys, or duffel bags are not allowed.
thingsToCarry: Thermal Inner Wears (Both Upper and Lower)
Government Photo Identity Card (Passport, Aadhaar Card, Driving license or Voter ID)
thingsToCarryNotes: A small hiking bag is used only if the main bag is given to a porter or mule. It is also needed on the final day of the summit climb.
Rental gear like jackets, shoes, trek poles, headlamps, ponchos, and more is available at Sankri basecamp market.

discrepancies: Cover states "5-6 DAYS", Overview states "6Days", and the itinerary runs to Day 7 (a conditional buffer day). Duration recorded as the Overview value, "6 Days"; nights are not stated anywhere.
No price appears on the cover; the three fares are printed on the "How to Book" page.
Brief itinerary Day 4 gives trek as 12km/6-7hrs; the Day 4 page gives 12–14 km.
Brief itinerary Day 2 reads "Driver 19km/1.5hrs" (apparent typo for "Drive").
Day 5 and Day 6 pages give no distances or durations; the brief itinerary does.
Things to Carry note mentions "the final day of the summit climb", but this trek has no summit day.
Gallery page shows Kashmir Great Lakes photographs rather than Har Ki Dun.
